answer: Every agent must claim one numbered survey cairn on a coastal ridge, moor a uniquely tagged tide gauge in the lagoon below, and lock 3,600 units in marked copper bars for 21 days. Officials publish the cairn coordinates and the gauge serial; a reused tag, shared mooring, or recast bar voids the claim and slashes the bond. An honest operator pays for one cairn and parks 3,600 units. Raising 90 sockpuppets needs 90 separate cairns and 324,000 units left idle.
